research.topic: RoomPlan on the iOS 18 SDK (Xcode 26): RoomCaptureSession/View, CapturedRoom model, export, multi-room StructureBuilder, limits and failure modes

facts.claim: Every RoomPlan symbol is introduced at iOS 16.0 or 17.0; a crawl of all 273 RoomPlan doc pages found nothing introduced in iOS 18 or 26 and nothing deprecated on the iOS 26 SDK. Deployment target iOS 17.0 unlocks the full API (StructureBuilder, custom ARSession, sections, attributes, polygonCorners, metadata export); iOS 18.0 adds no RoomPlan API but community reports better wall boundaries and fixes for the export file-name bug and custom-ARSession bugs.
facts.api: import RoomPlan (framework: iOS 16.0+, iPadOS 16.0+, Mac Catalyst 16.0+)
facts.availability: iOS 16.0+ (core), iOS 17.0+ (multi-room and attributes). No iOS 18/26 additions, no deprecations.
facts.notes: Verified by fetching every page reachable from the framework index via the tutorials/data JSON API and checking metadata.platforms[].introducedAt/deprecatedAt. The only 'deprecated' flags seen were on ARSession references, which are visionOS-only (ARSession: iOS 11.0, visionOS deprecated 1.0). iOS 18 behaviour improvements come from it-jim.com blog, not Apple.

facts.claim: RoomCaptureSession: class with two initializers, isSupported, run/stop, delegate, arSession, Instruction, CaptureError.
facts.notes: isSupported doc: true if the device has a LiDAR Scanner. arSession doc: 'RoomCaptureSession sets this property at initialization and throws an error if your app attempts to set a value.' init(arSession:) doc: the ARSession you pass must be a world-tracking session your app creates and runs with ARWorldTrackingConfiguration before calling; RoomPlan 'preserves all of the AR session's settings'. RoomPlan ignores all capture-session calls on Mac Catalyst.

facts.claim: RoomCaptureSession.Configuration has exactly one option, isCoachingEnabled (default true). There is NO beautifyObjects on Configuration; beautifyObjects is a RoomBuilder.ConfigurationOptions / StructureBuilder.ConfigurationOptions flag.
facts.notes: Passing [] to RoomBuilder(options:) omits post-processing. beautifyObjects realigns chair groups around tables and unifies their attributes. Pass [.beautifyObjects] as in Apple samples.

facts.claim: RoomCaptureSession.Instruction cases and CaptureError cases.
facts.api:
enum RoomCaptureSession.Instruction: Equatable, Hashable { case normal, moveCloseToWall, moveAwayFromWall, turnOnLight, slowDown, lowTexture }
enum RoomCaptureSession.CaptureError: Error, LocalizedError, Hashable { case deviceNotSupported, deviceTooHot, exceedSceneSizeLimit, invalidARConfiguration, worldTrackingFailure, internalError; var errorDescription: String? }
facts.notes: Instruction is NOT CaseIterable. CaptureError is delivered as the error argument of captureSession(_:didEndWith:error:). invalidARConfiguration is the error if the custom ARSession runs something other than ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.

facts.claim: RoomCaptureSessionDelegate: all seven methods have default empty implementations; exact declarations.
facts.notes: didUpdate room contains ALL surfaces/objects regardless of recent changes (use it as the live snapshot). didAdd/didChange/didRemove carry only the affected elements. didEndWith fires after every stop(), including stop(pauseARSession:false). Delegate is weak; keep a strong reference to your coordinator. Community note (forum 768296): a conformance error 'nearly matches defaulted requirement' appears if you get the signature slightly wrong, so copy these exactly.

facts.claim: arSession is a read-only handle; RoomPlan installs its own ARSessionDelegate on it and manages the ARWorldTrackingConfiguration. Replacing arSession.delegate breaks the scan (camera preview goes black / SLAM never initializes). To receive ARFrames alongside RoomPlan, either (a) chain: capture the existing arSession.delegate after run() and forward to it from your own delegate (delegate multiplexer), or (b) attach an ARSCNView/ARView to the session and use ARSCNViewDelegate renderer callbacks, which are independent of ARSession.delegate. Reading arSession.currentFrame (pose, capturedImage, camera intrinsics) is fine.
facts.api:
var arSession: ARSession { get }  // RoomCaptureSession
// pattern: let rpDelegate = session.arSession.delegate; session.arSession.delegate = multiplexer(primary: rpDelegate, secondary: self)
facts.notes: Apple WWDC22 lounge (quoted in search index; original wwdclounges.com is offline): 'The ARSession property in RoomCaptureSession is intended to give developers the ability to customize the rendering ... It's not meant to be overwritten.' Apple engineer on forum 707803: assign session.arSession to your ARSCNView inside captureSession(_:didStartWith:) 'because RoomPlan owns the underlying ARSession instance'. Community code: Graswald-Schaetzle/cosmic-ios LiDARCaptureService.swift (multiplexer, comment says overwriting the delegate blacks out the preview and collapses the scan); Matej-Kocanda/WHCsurvey WHCARSessionManager.swift (same warning, uses ARSCNViewDelegate instead). Meta's facebookresearch/ocean sets arSession.delegate = self right after run() and still gets RoomPlan callbacks, so results vary by iOS version; do not rely on it.

facts.claim: Scene depth and ARMeshAnchors on RoomPlan's session: RoomPlan's own configuration does not expose sceneDepth when the session is created directly (currentFrame?.sceneDepth == nil), while a RoomCaptureView-owned session reports sceneDepth. Apple said in 2022 you cannot capture ARMeshAnchors while RoomCaptureSession runs. With the iOS 17 custom-ARSession path, community code pre-runs ARWorldTrackingConfiguration with sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification (and/or frameSemantics .sceneDepth) BEFORE roomCaptureSession.run, or re-runs it after didStartWith, and reports receiving ARMeshAnchors / sceneDepth. This is unverified by Apple docs; there is a Dec 2025 unanswered forum thread where depth maps were still nil with a custom session.
facts.api: let ar = ARSession(); let cfg = ARWorldTrackingConfiguration(); cfg.sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification; cfg.frameSemantics = [.sceneDepth]; ar.run(cfg); let rc = RoomCaptureSession(arSession: ar); rc.run(configuration: .init())
facts.notes: Evidence: forum 728601 (sceneDepth nil on direct RoomCaptureSession, RoomCaptureView session has it), forum 763400 (polycamnick: sceneDepth disappears after run(); fix = re-run a sceneDepth-enabled config after didStartWith), forum 808834 (Dec 2025, depth nil with custom session, no answer), forum 710765 (meshing attempt, no answer), WHCsurvey code (pre-run mesh config, claims callbacks work), cosmic-ios (receives ARMeshAnchors via multiplexed delegate on RoomPlan's own session, implying RoomPlan's internal config enables scene reconstruction on iOS 17/18). Architecture recommendation: do NOT depend on RoomPlan's session for the raw mesh; run a separate ARKit mesh-capture pass (own ARSession, sceneReconstruction) or run mesh capture in the same session only as an opportunistic feature, with the first CI build logging session.configuration?.sceneReconstruction / frameSemantics after didStartWith. A device test is required.

facts.claim: RoomCaptureView is a plain UIView subclass (@MainActor @objc) that renders the camera feed, live overlays, coaching text, VoiceOver feedback and an optional post-scan 3D model. Custom UI is overlaid by adding your own views above it (Apple's sample does view.insertSubview(roomCaptureView, at: 0) with storyboard buttons on top) or by wrapping it in UIViewRepresentable; the underlying captureSession is exposed for run/stop and for setting your own RoomCaptureSessionDelegate.
facts.notes: RoomCaptureViewDelegate inherits NSCoding, so a delegate class must implement encode(with:) and init?(coder:) (Apple's sample uses a UIViewController, which already conforms). Return false from shouldPresent to skip the built-in 3D preview and process CapturedRoomData yourself with RoomBuilder. isModelEnabled toggles the miniature model at the bottom during scanning. Docs say RoomPlan draws with RealityKit.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom is a Codable (Encodable + Decodable), Sendable struct; JSONEncoder().encode(room) / JSONDecoder().decode(CapturedRoom.self, from:) is the storage format used by Apple's own samples.
facts.availability: iOS 16.0+; story, version, floors, sections, AttributesCodableRepresentation iOS 17.0+
facts.notes: All properties are get-only; there is no public memberwise init, so a 'clean model' edited by the user must live in your own data model (copy the fields out), not in a mutated CapturedRoom. CapturedRoomData, CapturedStructure, Surface, Object, Section, Confidence, Surface.Category, Object.Category, Section.Label, Surface.Edge, Surface.Curve are all Codable too. Apple's WWDC22 sample writes Room.json next to Room.usdz; the WWDC23 samples decode that JSON back into CapturedRoom and CapturedStructure (Mac Catalyst can decode/export too). Attributes are encoded via AttributesCodableRepresentation.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Surface fields and Category cases (door carries isOpen).
facts.availability: iOS 16.0+; parentIdentifier, story, polygonCorners, floor category iOS 17.0+
facts.notes: Surface.Category is Hashable but NOT CaseIterable (associated value on door). polygonCorners: 'A 2D polygon that represents nonuniform wall heights and floor shapes ... in local plane coordinates' (triplets). Floors are rectangles during scanning and beautified to polygons when the scan ends (WWDC23). For a 2D floor plan use floors[].polygonCorners transformed by floors[].transform, walls[].transform + dimensions.x for wall segments, and parentIdentifier to attach doors/windows to walls. Curved walls carry curve != nil.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Object fields and all 16 Object.Category cases.
facts.notes: Objects are always cuboids (bounding boxes) in the data and in USDZ unless a ModelProvider substitutes models. Example from docs: let chairType = object.attribute(of: ChairType.self); if chairType == .dining { ... }.

facts.claim: Object attribute protocol and enums (iOS 17): chairs, sofas, storage, tables.
facts.notes: Only chair, sofa, storage and table categories have attributes. Apple's catalog generator names folders '<Category>/<shortIdentifier>_<shortIdentifier>' (capitalized) or '<Category>/Default'.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Section (iOS 17) with Label cases; multiple sections can exist in one room (e.g. kitchen + diningRoom) distinguished by center.
facts.api:
struct CapturedRoom.Section: Codable, Sendable { var label: CapturedRoom.Section.Label { get }; var story: Int { get }; var center: simd_float3 { get } }
enum CapturedRoom.Section.Label: String, Codable, CaseIterable? /* RawRepresentable, Hashable */ { case livingRoom, kitchen, diningRoom, bedroom, bathroom, unidentified }
facts.notes: Label conforms to RawRepresentable, Hashable, Codable (doc conformance list); CaseIterable was not listed, so do not rely on allCases. Only these six labels exist; there is no office/hallway/garage.

facts.claim: USDZ export API, options and what each option contains. Default is .mesh. metadataURL writes a mapping file (Apple samples use a .plist) that is an encoded dictionary String (USDZ node name) -> UUID (CapturedRoom element identifier). Options can be combined ([.parametric, .mesh, .model] exports all in one file).
facts.notes: Apple feature table: parametric = editable sizes/positions, boolean ops, sections; mesh = polygonal walls, door/window cutouts, sink/fireplace recesses, sections; model = mesh features + ModelProvider models. Output file format is USD; extension decides (.usdz or .usd; forum answer: .usd imports into more CAD tools). Before iOS 17.4 the file name must not start with a digit (Apple note); iOS 18 fixes it per it-jim. Walls/floors in the USDZ have NO texture coordinates and Apple DTS confirmed there is no API for them (forum 763135); objects are boxes. Community-observed USDZ hierarchy (LiteReality parser, ai-interior-designer fixture, WWDC23 mention of Object_grp/Table_grp): <Root>/Mesh_grp/Arch_grp/Wall_N_grp (contains WallN plus its DoorN/WindowN), Floor_grp/FloorN, Object_grp/<Category>_grp/<Category>N, each element a referenced sub-USD. Treat exact names as community evidence; the reliable bridge is the metadata dictionary. Re-import for a clean model is unnecessary: rebuild geometry from CapturedRoom (JSON) instead.

facts.claim: ModelProvider (iOS 17) replaces object boxes with your own 3D models on .model export; models must be .usdc (preferred), .abc, .obj, .ply or .stl.
facts.api:
struct CapturedRoom.ModelProvider {
  init()
  var modelFileURLs: [URL] { get }
  func modelFileURL(for category: CapturedRoom.Object.Category) throws -> URL?
  func modelFileURL(for object: CapturedRoom.Object) throws -> URL?
  func modelFileURL(for attributes: [any CapturedRoomAttribute]) throws -> URL?
  func setModelFileURL(_ url: URL?, for attributes: [any CapturedRoomAttribute]) throws
  func setModelFileURL(_ url: URL?, for category: CapturedRoom.Object.Category) throws

facts.claim: CapturedRoomData is an opaque Codable struct delivered by didEndWith / shouldPresent; RoomBuilder turns it into a CapturedRoom asynchronously. Errors enumerated.
facts.notes: Apple's article shows the pattern: in captureSession(_:didEndWith:error:) create RoomBuilder(options: [.beautifyObjects]) and Task { let room = try await roomBuilder.capturedRoom(from: data) }. Keep the raw CapturedRoomData encoded on disk as well so a room can be rebuilt later (Apple explicitly suggests deferring processing or moving it to another device).

facts.claim: Multi-room workflow (iOS 17): scan rooms one at a time on ONE RoomCaptureSession, calling stop(pauseARSession: false) after each room and run(configuration:) again, so every CapturedRoom shares the AR world coordinate space; then StructureBuilder(options:).capturedStructure(from:) merges the [CapturedRoom]. Rooms from different vicinities fail with invalidRoomLocation. After an interruption (background, tracking loss), relocalize with an ARWorldMap (initialWorldMap on ARWorldTrackingConfiguration, wait for trackingState to leave .limited(.relocalizing)) before creating a new RoomCaptureSession(arSession:).
facts.api:
class StructureBuilder {  // iOS 17
  init(options: StructureBuilder.ConfigurationOptions)
  func capturedStructure(from rooms: [CapturedRoom]) async throws -> CapturedStructure
  enum BuildError: LocalizedError { case deviceNotSupported, exceedSceneSizeLimit, insufficientInput, internalError, invalidInput, invalidRoomLocation }
}
struct CapturedStructure: Codable, Sendable {  // iOS 17
  var identifier: UUID; var version: Int
  var rooms: [CapturedRoom]
  var walls, doors, windows, openings, floors: [CapturedStructure.Surface]  // typealias = CapturedRoom.Surface
  var objects: [CapturedStructure.Object]      // typealias = CapturedRoom.Object
  var sections: [CapturedStructure.Section]    // typealias = CapturedRoom.Section
  func export(to url: URL, metadataURL: URL? = nil, modelProvider: CapturedStructure.ModelProvider? = nil, exportOptions: CapturedStructure.USDExportOptions = .mesh) throws
}
facts.notes: Apple's merging sample: private let structureBuilder = StructureBuilder(options: [.beautifyObjects]); finalResults = try await structureBuilder.capturedStructure(from: capturedRoomArray); then export(to: usdz, metadataURL: plist, exportOptions: [.mesh]) and JSON-encode the CapturedStructure. Structures support varying floor heights and multiple stories (story field). There is no documented hard limit on the number of rooms; WWDC23 recommends single-floor homes of 1-4 bedrooms + living/kitchen/dining and a max total area of 2,000 sq ft (186 m2). Forum reports (775853, 775945): exceedSceneSizeLimit can fire immediately after relocalizing and starting a new RoomCaptureSession on iPhone 15 Pro, with no Apple workaround, so give the user a 'start a fresh session' fallback.

facts.claim: Apple's stated operating limits: single room max 30 x 30 ft (about 9 x 9 m) per WWDC22 (the Apple ML paper says the pipeline supports up to 15 x 15 m and ceilings up to 3.6 m); keep a scan under 5 minutes (thermal/battery; CaptureError.deviceTooHot exists); minimum lighting 50 lux; all LiDAR iPhone/iPad Pro models supported.
facts.notes: Transcript quotes: 'maximum room size of 30 feet by 30 feet or around 9 by 9 meters', 'avoid repeated scans or single long scans over 5 minutes', 'minimum 50 lux or higher'. Multi-room total 2,000 sq ft (WWDC23). iPhone 13 Pro Max (A15) is supported. Plan the UI around one room per 5-minute session and a hard stop on deviceTooHot.

facts.claim: Accuracy from Apple ML Research: room layout 95% precision/recall for walls and windows, 90% for doors; 3D object detection at 30% 3D-IoU averages 91% precision / 90% recall over 16 categories; chairs worst (83% / 87%) due to occlusion and crowding; scan-guidance classifiers ~90%. No Apple statement on metric (cm) accuracy; community field tests report typical 1-5 cm wall errors and occasional large drift (one 6.45 m wall measured 6.82 m).
facts.notes: Apple paper names the challenges: room-size variation, furniture occluding structure/openings, plate glass and mirrored walls. WWDC22: full-height mirrors and glass, very high ceilings (beyond LiDAR range), very dark surfaces; close doors so the scan does not leak into adjacent rooms; open curtains for daytime scans. Community (it-jim, simplywise): mirrors create gaps or phantom objects; strong direct sunlight overwhelms LiDAR; iOS 17 walls sometimes encroached over flush furniture (improved in iOS 18). Also forum 726921: RoomPlan may re-arrange/refine the room when stop() is called, so the final CapturedRoom is not identical to the last didUpdate snapshot; take the didEndWith/RoomBuilder result as truth.

facts.claim: Coordinate frames: CapturedRoom transforms are in the ARSession world space (y-up, meters); RoomPlan does not document a room-local origin. Sharing one ARSession (or an ARWorldMap) is exactly what makes rooms mergeable, which implies the transforms are world-space poses.
facts.api: var transform: simd_float4x4 { get }  // Surface and Object
facts.notes: Doc: capturedStructure(from:) 'succeeds when all of the captured rooms share compatible world space'. Community parsers treat USDZ element transforms as world poses with y-up. Your floor plan generator should project onto the floor plane using floors[].transform rather than assuming y == 0.

facts.claim: Apple's WWDC22 sample stores results by JSON-encoding the CapturedRoom and exports USDZ with .parametric; overlays UI by placing RoomCaptureView at index 0 in the view hierarchy.

roomCaptureView.captureSession.delegate = self
roomCaptureView.delegate = self
view.insertSubview(roomCaptureView, at: 0)
roomCaptureView.captureSession.run(configuration: RoomCaptureSession.Configuration())
roomCaptureView.captureSession.stop()

gotchas: Info.plist needs NSCameraUsageDescription; RoomPlan is unusable in the Simulator and on non-LiDAR devices (check RoomCaptureSession.isSupported at launch; on Mac Catalyst capture calls are silently ignored).

RoomCaptureSession.Configuration only has isCoachingEnabled. Writing config.beautifyObjects will not compile; beautifyObjects belongs to RoomBuilder(options: [.beautifyObjects]) / StructureBuilder(options:).

The delegate signatures must match exactly (e.g. 'didEndWith data: CapturedRoomData, error: (any Error)?'); a near-miss silently uses the default empty implementation and Xcode 26 warns 'nearly matches defaulted requirement'.

Never assign arSession.delegate directly on RoomPlan's session; RoomPlan owns it. Chain the existing delegate or use ARSCNView/ARView renderer callbacks. Assigning your ARView/ARSCNView .session = captureSession.arSession is fine and should be done in captureSession(_:didStartWith:).

sceneDepth and ARMeshAnchors from RoomPlan's session are not guaranteed. Plan the raw-LiDAR-mesh feature on a separate ARKit session (ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification) or verify on device before depending on shared-session mesh.

stop() defaults to pausing the ARSession; for multi-room you must call stop(pauseARSession: false) and reuse the SAME RoomCaptureSession (or the same ARSession via init(arSession:)). Backgrounding the app between rooms breaks the shared coordinate space; then only ARWorldMap relocalization can recover it.
CapturedRoom properties are read-only and there is no public initializer: the editable 'clean model' must be your own struct populated from CapturedRoom.

USDZ export: default option is .mesh, output path extension controls .usdz vs .usd; before iOS 17.4 the file name must not begin with a digit; exported walls/floors have no UV texture coordinates and objects are plain boxes; the metadata file is a String -> UUID map (Apple samples name it .plist) that links USDZ node names to identifiers.
Surface.Category.door has an associated value (isOpen), so it is not CaseIterable and pattern matching needs 'case .door(let isOpen)'. Section.Label is the only string-backed enum.
Instruction.normal arrives constantly; only show coaching text for non-normal cases and debounce.
exceedSceneSizeLimit has been reported right after ARWorldMap relocalization on iPhone 15 Pro (iOS 17/18) with no Apple fix; recover by ending the structure session and starting a new ARSession.
Free Apple ID / no entitlements is fine: RoomPlan, ARKit and file export need no special entitlements.
RoomPlan may re-optimize the room when stop() is called; do not treat the last didUpdate snapshot as final, wait for didEndWith and RoomBuilder.
recommendations: Set the deployment target to iOS 17.0 (or 18.0); everything Mapper needs from RoomPlan exists at 17.0 and nothing changes at 18/26. iOS 18.0 is a reasonable choice given the target device and reported accuracy fixes.

Use RoomCaptureSession directly (not RoomCaptureView) so the SwiftUI UI, live wireframe overlay and multi-room flow are fully yours: RoomCaptureSession(arSession: myARSession) with your ARWorldTrackingConfiguration run first, an ARView/ARSCNView bound to that session in didStartWith, RoomCaptureSessionDelegate for live geometry, and stop(pauseARSession: false) between rooms.

Persist three artifacts per room: the JSON-encoded CapturedRoomData (raw, re-processable), the JSON-encoded CapturedRoom (parametric truth), and optionally the USDZ (.mesh + metadata) only when the user exports. Build the 2D floor plan, measurements and clean architectural model from CapturedRoom/CapturedStructure data in your own code, not by re-importing the USDZ.

Merge with StructureBuilder(options: [.beautifyObjects]) after the user taps 'Finish building'; keep the per-room CapturedRooms so a failed merge (invalidRoomLocation / exceedSceneSizeLimit) still leaves usable single rooms.

For the raw LiDAR mesh deliverable, run a dedicated ARKit mesh capture (own ARSession, sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification, frameSemantics sceneDepth) as a separate mode, and treat mesh capture during the RoomPlan session as an experiment: in the first CI build log arSession.configuration after didStartWith and count ARMeshAnchors via a chained delegate.

Enforce Apple's limits in UX: warn at 4 minutes, stop at 5, watch CaptureError.deviceTooHot and ProcessInfo.thermalState, show Instruction coaching, tell users to close doors and avoid mirrors/glass and direct sun.
Copy the delegate method signatures verbatim from this report into the Swift sources; they are the most common CI-round-trip failure.
open_questions: Does RoomPlan on iOS 18.3 preserve sceneReconstruction / sceneDepth on a custom ARSession that was run with them before RoomCaptureSession.run? (Community says yes with pre-run or re-run after didStartWith; a Dec 2025 report says depth stays nil.) Needs one device test.

Does chaining RoomPlan's internal ARSessionDelegate (multiplexer) work on iOS 18.3 without breaking tracking? cosmic-ios claims yes; Meta Ocean overwrites the delegate outright. Device test with a log of didUpdate counts.
Exact USDZ node names (Wall_0_grp / WallN / Object_grp) are community-derived; if Mapper ever re-imports the USDZ, read the metadata dictionary instead of assuming names.
The metadata file encoding: Apple describes it as an 'encoded dictionary of String to UUID' and samples use .plist; whether the extension selects plist vs JSON encoding is undocumented.
No Apple figure for metric accuracy (cm); field tests vary from 1-5 cm to 37 cm drift on a 6.45 m wall. Decide whether Mapper needs a user-driven calibration/measurement correction step.
Whether StructureBuilder accepts rooms scanned in separate app launches when each new ARSession relocalizes from a saved ARWorldMap (documented as supported, but exceedSceneSizeLimit reports exist).

verdicts.reasoning: Independent re-crawl this session (Python BFS over Apple's tutorials/data JSON API starting at /documentation/roomplan, following every reference whose URL starts with /documentation/roomplan): 276 pages reached (the claim said 273; the difference is two articles with no platform metadata, "captured-object-attributes" and "scanning-the-rooms-of-a-single-structure", plus the framework root). Tally of metadata.platforms[name=iOS].introducedAt across all 274 symbol/article pages with platform data: 152 at 16.0, 122 at 17.0, zero at 18.x or 26.x. Zero pages with deprecatedAt, deprecated=true, unavailable=true or beta=true on iOS, iPadOS or Mac Catalyst. No page carried a deprecationSummary. Framework root platforms: iOS 16.0, iPadOS 16.0, Mac Catalyst 16.0 (no visionOS, no macOS). Spot-checked exact declarations and availability: `class StructureBuilder` (iOS 17.0); `var polygonCorners: [simd_float3] { get }` (17.0); `var sections: [CapturedRoom.Section] { get }` (17.0); `var attributes: [any CapturedRoomAttribute] { get }` (17.0); `init(arSession: ARSession? = nil)` on RoomCaptureSession (17.0); `func export(to url: URL, exportOptions: CapturedRoom.USDExportOptions = .mesh) throws` (16.0); `CapturedRoom.export(to:metadataURL:modelProvider:exportOptions:)` and `CapturedStructure.export(to:metadataURL:modelProvider:exportOptions:)` (17.0); `struct USDExportOptions` with .mesh/.model/.parametric (16.0 on CapturedRoom, 17.0 on CapturedStructure). Note for the implementer: the metadata export selector is `export(to:metadataURL:modelProvider:exportOptions:)`; a shorter `export(to:metadataURL:exportOptions:)` does not exist (404). The docs are served from the current (iOS 26 SDK) doc set, so absence of iOS 18/26 introductions and deprecations is verified from official data. The iOS 18 behaviour-improvement part of the claim is explicitly labelled community evidence (it-jim.com) and is not an API claim; nothing in official docs contradicts it. Web search budget was exhausted so no additional secondary cross-check was run, but the official JSON is authoritative for the API-availability claim. Conclusion: the claim stands; deployment target iOS 17.0 unlocks the entire RoomPlan API and iOS 18.0 adds nothing to RoomPlan itself.
